# Togakushi Ninja Museum戸隠流忍法資料館
## Enter the realm of ninjas
The Togakushi Ninja Museum in Togakushi, northwest of Nagano City, is dedicated to the ancient and stealthy art of ninjutsu and the warriors who trained in the surrounding mountains.

### Don't Miss
- Finding your way through the museum's special Ninja House

## How to Get There
The museum is an easy bus ride from Nagano Station.

### Explore the way of Ninjutsu
The Togakushi Ninja Museum is devoted to the local Togakushi school of ninjutsu which started in the 12th century.

### Get up close with weapons only seen on the big screen
Spread over several reloated and resotred buildings, the Togakushi Ninja Museum lets you delve into ninja history with a variety of exhibits and activities. Their displays of traditional weaponry include katana (Japanese swords).

### Visit the ninja house
A “ninja house” in an adjacent building is a museum highlight. The house is full of traps and secret passageways; once inside, it's a veritable labyrinth that's notoriously tough to get out of. Once you finally escape, sneak over to the target range and try out your shuriken throwing skills.

The Museum of Togakushi Folklore on the property houses a wide collection of antiques and artifacts used by the locals in days gone by.

![](https://res.cloudinary.com/jnto/image/upload/w_750,h_503,fl_lossy,f_auto/v1519788767/nagano/Nagano2833_2)

### Ninja fun for the little ones
This ninja theme park lets kids don ninja outfits and slink their way through attractions like forested adventure playgrounds, climbing walls, and a blow dart range.

## Enter the realm of ninjas

The Togakushi Ninja Museum in Togakushi, northwest of Nagano City, is dedicated to the ancient and stealthy art of ninjutsu and the warriors who trained in the surrounding mountains.

### Don't Miss

- Finding your way through the museum's special Ninja House
- Testing out your shuriken throwing skills

## How to Get There

The museum is an easy bus ride from Nagano Station.

The number 70 and 71 buses bound for Togakushi will take you to the Togakushi Okushairiguchi bus stop just across from the museum.

### Explore the way of Ninjutsu

The Togakushi Ninja Museum is devoted to the local Togakushi school of ninjutsu which started in the 12th century. Practitioners of this shadow art called Togakushi, and its once inaccessible mountains, home. The mountains had long been inhabited by Buddhist-shaman ascetics known as yamabushi, and aspects of their philosophy found their way into the Togakushi school.

### Get up close with weapons only seen on the big screen

Spread over several reloated and resotred buildings, the Togakushi Ninja Museum lets you delve into ninja history with a variety of exhibits and activities. Their displays of traditional weaponry include katana (Japanese swords). Blade-like metal throwing stars known as shuriken are laid out in more shapes and sizes than you'd think possible.

![](https://res.cloudinary.com/jnto/image/upload/w_670,h_450,fl_lossy,f_auto/v1519788775/nagano/Nagano2833_4)

![](https://res.cloudinary.com/jnto/image/upload/w_670,h_450,fl_lossy,f_auto/v1519788771/nagano/Nagano2833_3)

### Learn all about the hidden history of the ninja

While the weaponry certainly catches the eye, much of the ninja's craft involved espionage, infiltration, and generally going unseen. Escape was key, and contrary to ninja movies, violence was typically avoided.

Information boards illustrating these arts are on display, as is ninja clothing and gear that remind visitors the ninjas were human, too. The museum walls are covered with photographs of ninja demonstrating their craft.

### Visit the ninja house

A “ninja house” in an adjacent building is a museum highlight. The house is full of traps and secret passageways; once inside, it's a veritable labyrinth that's notoriously tough to get out of. Once you finally escape, sneak over to the target range and try out your shuriken throwing skills.

The Museum of Togakushi Folklore on the property houses a wide collection of antiques and artifacts used by the locals in days gone by.

![](https://res.cloudinary.com/jnto/image/upload/w_750,h_503,fl_lossy,f_auto/v1519788767/nagano/Nagano2833_2)

### Ninja fun for the little ones

Kids will enjoy the Kids Ninja Village 3.4 kilometers down the road from The Togakushi Ninja Museum. This ninja theme park lets kids don ninja outfits and slink their way through attractions like forested adventure playgrounds, climbing walls, and a blow dart range. They offer game-style, shuriken-throwing courses.

May 2026









This facility is located on the opposite side of the road from the inner shrine of Togakushi-jinja Shrine, and although there are certainly folk museums and archives, aside from those facilities, the main facility here is already a ninja to Kuriyashiki.

The Karakuri Yashiki in the nearby village of Chibikko Ninja had tried it once, about seven years ago, and I thought it wouldn't be too difficult to escape, but I ended up in a complete cul-de-sac along the way.

I'm forced to roam around the same place in circles, and although I know the direction of the exit, I can't find a mechanism to get through to the exit.

When the exasperated child gave up and called for help, he said, 'I see, there's no way you can understand this until you soften your head and change your mind.'

There's only one place I can get help, and then I'll have to get out on my own, but I've had a lot of fun with a couple of hard-hitting knots.

The fact that there's phone help in that place is probably because there are so many people stuck there, and conversely, it would be quite exhilarating to be able to completely solve that trick.

It's important to note that if you happen to be in the same place as someone else and you see someone else unwind, you'll get quite excited, so you should avoid encounters with people so that doesn't happen.

Even when we made it out safely and left the mansion, there was a little surprise waiting for us, and we were truly entertained by both adults and children.

[thelonious22](https://www.tripadvisor.com/ClientLink?value=ZUU2Xy9Qcm9maWxlL3RoZWxvbmlvdXMyMl9jd0Q%3D)·
Aug 2019









Togakure Ninpo Museum complex, located across from the upper Togakushi Shrine entrance, is divided into three separate museums. First is just a collection of old tools and handicrafts that didn’t take more than ten minutes to look at. Second is a ninja museum with actual collection of weapons and old photographs showing the training which was quite interesting. The complex ground also has a handful of interactive areas including a suspension bridge, shaky two story pagoda, and a mini rope course. Visitors can also throw ninja stars for a fee. The highlight, which should also be the last stop, is the ninja house full of trick doors. Visitors have the option to attempt to walk around the house on their own, although staff are available to guide you through. With a maze portion at the end, it would’ve been quite difficult to find the exit on our own. The variety of trick doors we went through kept the entire walk through interesting.

For educational part, there's museum which tells the history of Togakushi ninja, knowledge of ninja (like weapons, skills, training etc.) and the history of this place around. We couldn't understand all Japanese but we could grasp the brief idea so we learned a lot.

Recommend this to everyone.

![20024_ext_01_en_0_L-1](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/Imported_Blog_Media/20024_ext_01_en_0_L-1.jpg?width=1600&height=1064&name=20024_ext_01_en_0_L-1.jpg)

Main Visual ©Nagano Convention & Visitors Bureau

Less than an hour away from central Nagano City, Togakushi is a haven of outdoor activities such as trekking, snowshoeing, cross-country skiing, birdwatching, and camping.

It is also a spiritual destination, known as a “power spot” in Japan thanks to its five Shinto Shrines surrounded by majestic mountains and forests.

But that’s not all hiding in Togakushi. In fact, this once remote location was a training ground for ninja, who practiced a unique variety of martial arts called Togakure-ryu. Even today, there are places around Togakushi where you can get in touch with its ninja past.

Whether looking to train seriously, snap some photos of the kids in cute outfits or get away from the city, a Togakushi ninja experience is sure to enrich any Nagano trip.

Five Ways to Get in Touch with Ninja in Togakushi

- [The History of Togakushi's Ninja](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/id20024#page01)
- [Ninja Experiences in Togakushi](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/id20024#page02)

  - [Ninja Training](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/id20024#page05)
  - [Hiking and Mountain Climbing in Togakushi](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/id20024#page06)
  - [Eat like a Ninja](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/id20024#page07)
- [Accommodation in Togakushi](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/id20024#page08)

## The History of Togakushi's Ninja

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/Imported_Blog_Media/51000733324_97a41f7940_k-small.jpg)Mt. Togakushi seen from Kagami Pond

Togakushi’s name, meaning “Hidden Door,” comes from one of Japan’s Shinto legends. In that legend, the sun goddess Amaterasu and her brother, the god of storms and seas, argued frequently. One day, Amaterasu had enough and hid in a cave, plunging the world into darkness. The other gods danced outside the cave to coax her out until Amaterasu became jealous. When she cracked open the door, another god flung the door away. The door landed in Nagano and became present-day Mt. Togakushi.

Later, Mt. Togakushi became a center for Shugendo, a mix of Shinto and Buddhist religious beliefs whose followers sought supernatural powers through severe asceticism. Among other practices, worshipers meditated under ice-cold waterfalls, walked in the snow, and fasted in caves for weeks on end.

According to legend, the 12th century samurai warrior Daisuke Nishina combined samurai fighting styles with Shugendo to form Togakure-ryu Ninjutsu. The style has been passed on from master to master to this day. Today, around 20 dojos with 100 instructors teach Togakure-ryu Ninjutsu around Japan.

## Ninja Experiences in Togakushi

### The Togakushi Ninja Museum

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/Imported_Blog_Media/DSCN1719-small.jpg)Inside the Togakure Ninja Museum. On the right is the Karakuri Yashiki, a fun house full of hidden doors and secrets.

To learn more about the history of Togakushi's ninja and see the tools they used, visit the [Togakushi Ninja Museum](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/topics_detail6/id=12288). English information is limited, but the museum contains hundreds of fascinating artifacts about the ninja and life in Togakushi Village. Visitors can also try their hand at Ninja skills, such as Shuriken throwing near the exhibit.

Another highlight of the Ninja museum is the Ninja House rigged with hidden doors, secret passages, and booby traps that are a fun experience for kids and adults alike.

### Kids' Ninja Village

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/Imported_Blog_Media/%E3%83%81%E3%83%93%E3%83%83%E5%AD%90%E5%BF%8D%E8%80%85%E6%9D%91%E2%91%A2-small.jpg)One of many obstacles courses found in the Kids' Ninja Village

©Nagano Convention & Visitors Bureau

The [Kids' Ninja Village](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/topics_detail6/id=12271) ( _Chibikko Ninja Mura_) is another great attraction for families. There are ninja outfits available for rent, and kids can go through various obstacle courses and challenges. There is a ropes course, jungle gym, rope towing across a pond, shuriken throwing, dart-blowing, a ninja house, and live demonstrations.

The park is only open from late April to late November.

### Ninja Training

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/Imported_Blog_Media/togakushi-ninja-training.jpg)Participants practice weapons such as staves and shuriken as well as grappling and other skills

For those serious about Ninja training, there are lessons available from authentic Togakure-ryu ninjutsu practitioners. Becoming a ninja takes thousands of hours, but this is an excellent option if you are curious, want to start down the path, or compare training methods. The ninja training covers basics such as stance, defensive tactics, and trying out some weapons used by ninja.

Please note: the instructors practice weekly and are serious about their training. This experience is geared towards visitors who have practiced martial arts or those seriously interested in Ninjutsu.

Contact [Togakushi Soba Yamaguchiya](https://www.togakushisoba.com/original10.html), whose owner is a ninja, to make a reservation. Make a reservation several days to weeks in advance to ensure availability.

### Hiking and Mountain Climbing in Togakushi

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/Imported_Blog_Media/IMGP6872-small.jpg)Hiking past 400-year-old cedars on the way to the Togakushi Okusha Shrine

Although not technically a form of ninja training, hiking is a great way to stay physically fit and channel your inner ninja. There are various hikes around the five shrines of Togakushi with loops of different lengths. Recommended sightseeing locations include Chusha Shrine, Okusha Shrine, Hokosha Shrine, Zuishinmon Gate, the Togakushi Forest Botanical Garden, and Kagami Pond. Stop by the Togakushi Tourist Information Center to pick up a map before walking.

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/Imported_Blog_Media/IMGP2428-small.jpg)Climbing one of Mt. Togakushi's many chain sections

For the greatest challenge, climb Mt. Togakushi. Originating near the Okusha Shrine, the trail winds up Mt. Togakushi with occasional steep passes necessitating chains for climbing. Near the summit, the trail goes over a famous knife-edge point with sharp drop-offs on each side. The path is around a 7-hour loop and requires serious hiking equipment, so please arrive prepared when planning to summit Mt. Togakushi. The trail is only open in the summer due to heavy snowfall.

### Eat Like a Ninja

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/Imported_Blog_Media/IMG_9697-small.jpeg)Ninja Soba set from Togakushi Soba Yamaguchiya

In Togakushi, even the food is connected to the ninja. Because Togakushi's mountainous terrain was not suited to rice cultivation, soba became the predominant food source. Soba was also a portable and nutritious food for ninjas and monks practicing in Togakushi's mountains. Nowadays, dozens of soba restaurants are scattered throughout Togakushi village. Cold noodles dipped in sauce with a side of tempura is refreshing in the summer, while piping a hot bowl of soba warms your whole body in the winter. Rumor has it that eating extra spicy Togakushi soba is even a form of ninja training.

## Accommodation in Togakushi

Although there are no major hotel chains in Togakushi, various ryokans, minshuku, and shukubos provide a unique accommodation experience. Although one can find ryokans and minshuku throughout Japan, a shukubo is a unique traditional pilgrim's lodging used to house worshipers. In addition, some Shinto priests operate shukubos, so you can participate in a Shinto cleansing ceremony in the morning.

## Conclusion

Togakushi is a hidden gem offering cultural, spiritual, natural, and culinary attractions year-round. Especially for those interested in ninja, Togakushi offers activities for all ages and physical abilities. To leave the beaten path and have a unique Nagano experience, make sure to add Togakushi to your next trip and become a ninja!

## Togakushi: Discover Nagano's Ninja Culture

![Togakushi Shrine](https://resources.matcha-jp.com/resize/720x2000/2026/06/03-265026.webp)

The path leading to Togakushi Shrine Okusha. Photo by Pixta

Ever since watching _Naruto_, I’ve been fascinated by ninjas. To me, they always carried an air of mystery, existing as a unique presence separate from the rest of the world.

So, when I visited Nagano, a trip to **Togakushi**—renowned as the home of the ninja—was absolutely mandatory.

The ninjas here belong to the Togakushi-ryu school, and all their secrets are hidden deep within the **Togakushi Ninja Museum** and the **Ninja Trick Mansion** (Karakuri Yashiki).

Besides the history-rich Togakushi Shrine, the Togakushi Ninja Museum is one of the best places to visit in Togakushi, a mountainous area in Nagano.

## Exploring the Togakushi Ninja Museum

![Togakushi Ninja Museum](https://resources.matcha-jp.com/resize/720x2000/2017/05/22-26950.webp)

When I first heard the word "museum," I pictured a small, standard building. To my surprise, it turned out to be more like a miniature ninja village divided into various activity zones.

Admission is 700 yen for adults and 500 yen for elementary and junior high school students.

![Togakushi Ninja Museum](https://resources.matcha-jp.com/resize/720x2000/2017/05/22-26951.webp)

Because our time was limited, we couldn't fit in the cultural exhibits, like the museum and the folklore pavilion.

My companion and I had only one goal in mind: head straight for the Ninja Trick Mansion and conquer it!

## Togakushi Ninja Trick Mansion: An Endless Stream of Ninja Experiences

![Togakushi Ninja Trick Mansion](https://resources.matcha-jp.com/resize/720x2000/2017/05/22-26952.webp)

Upon arriving at the Trick House, you first take off your shoes and place them on the rack, then show your ticket to head inside! The rules are simple, giving off a vibe very similar to a real-life escape room.

Each room is packed with layers of tricks and hidden mechanisms, featuring doors that look nothing like the ones we see in everyday life. If you can find the exits, break through the series of challenges, and ultimately escape the residence, your mission is a complete success.

It might seem bizarre, but this is exactly how a real ninja residence operates. Hidden doors are never out in the open; instead, they are cleverly concealed where you’d least expect them—blended into the walls, tucked behind hanging scrolls, or hidden beneath tea tables.

Even when an exit looks like a perfectly normal door, it won't open with a simple turn of a knob. To survive this mansion, you’ll need to let your imagination run wild and think outside the box!

![Togakushi Ninja Trick Mansion](https://resources.matcha-jp.com/resize/720x2000/2017/05/22-26953.webp)

Why go to the trouble of installing so many hidden doors? The answer lies in survival: they made escaping effortless while leaving enemies entirely disoriented.

In an authentic ninja home, weapons were strategically cached inside these secret passageways for a swift counterattack or a rapid retreat.

Legend has it that a single traditional residence could contain over a dozen hidden doors and traps—a true masterclass in calculated deception.

## 3D Maze, Hidden Doors, and Other Traps: Escape to Freedom

![Togakushi Ninja Trick Mansion](https://resources.matcha-jp.com/resize/720x2000/2017/05/22-26949.webp)

With multiple stages that ramp up in difficulty, the Togakushi Ninja Trick Mansion offers a thrilling and immersive challenge.

The most unique feature is the slanted room; the moment you step inside, you feel an instant wave of dizziness. Fortunately, as long as you avoid looking up and focus on the tatami mats on the floor, the sensation passes.

From there, you just have to work your way up the slope to reach the exit. This room is easily the most entertaining stage in the house and is perfect for a big group of friends to experience together.

## Practice Shuriken Throwing Techniques in the Ninja Dojo

![Togakushi Ninja Trick Mansion](https://resources.matcha-jp.com/resize/720x2000/2017/05/22-26954.webp)

Outside the Trick House, there is a shuriken-throwing dojo where visitors can try their hand at throwing ninja stars. Having tried it myself, I can honestly say it’s quite difficult!

![Togakushi Ninja Trick Mansion](https://resources.matcha-jp.com/resize/720x2000/2017/05/22-26955.webp)

The shuriken aren't heavy, but they really test your technique; hitting the target takes a lot of practice. Be sure to test your skills at the dojo and see if you have the natural talent to be a ninja!

## Enjoy Exploring the Togakushi Ninja Trick Mansion

We had an absolute blast at the Ninja Trick Mansion in Togakushi and can't wait to explore more of the ninja village next time.

Don't miss out on this exciting adventure—it's perfect for families with children and a total must-do for any true ninja fan!

Togakushi Ninja Museum is also known as The Togakure Ninpo Museum / Togakushi folk museum. It is devoted to the local Togakure school of the ninja. It is near the Togakushi Shrine in Nagano, Japan. 
There is the Museum of Togakushi Folklore. Ninja tools like Steel climbing claws, different sizes of Shurikens, Japanese swords, photos, furniture, clothing, and other Ninja-related documents are exhibited here. ## Where is Togakushi?

Togakushi is a heavily forested alpine area that takes its name from Mount Togakushi (1904m), which rises above the surrounding area and village. That area is quite a wide region covering many attractions but in order to get your bearings, let’s consider the centre of Togakushi to be the Togakushi Tourist Information Center. Located in the upper village, it is around 20KM / 40-minutes drive from [Nagano Station](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/?p=13523). Local bus services operate from Nagano Station to various points in Togakushi, taking 45 to 70-minutes depending on your exact destination. Togakushi village has an average elevation of around 1200 metres above sea level, blessing it with a cool climate through spring, summer and autumn, and very cold winter. Nestled within the larger [Myoko-Togakushi Renzan National Park](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/?p=55009), Togakushi covers a wide area and boasts some of Japan’s most important Shinto shrines, beautiful walking trails, abundant flora and fauna along with the nearest ski resort to Nagano Station, [Togakushi Ski Resort](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/activities/togakushi-ski-resort/).

### 1 / THE SHRINES OF TOGAKUSHI / all year round\*

![togakushi-edit](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/IMG_2656-683x1024-1.jpg)

Japan's native religion of Shintoism has a strong association with nature worship, which is on grand display in Togakushi. Spread through the forested mountains are five shrines making up the Shinto complex, connected by scenic trails.

![togakushi](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/3498227_m-2.jpg)

The two most prominent are the 'Okusha' (Upper Shrine) and the 'Chusha' (Middle Shrine). The Okusha is famous for its breathtaking avenue of giant cedars—many between 400 and 800 years old—leading up to a small shrine nestled at the base of the ragged peaks. Meanwhile, the Chusha, located in the center of the village, is the largest of the five. It features its own massive 800-year-old cedars and is conveniently surrounded by excellent 'soba' restaurants and bamboo craft shops. Whether you visit just one or hike between all five, the shrines offer a deeply spiritual and tranquil experience.

![togakushi-snowshoe-winter](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/ca98d676d1e0cdc2ab727b7016944a852_35742805_210630.jpg)

\*To access the Okusha or the Giant Cedar Avenue in winter - from December to March - you will need snowshoes, clothing and gear appropriate for winter hiking. ### 2 / SNOWSHOEING IN TOGAKUSHI / December to March

While Togakushi is famous for its lush green summers and vibrant autumns, winter transforms the region into a deep, snowy wonderland. From December to March, heavy snowfall blankets the area, making standard walking trails inaccessible. However, this opens up the perfect opportunity to explore the landscape by snowshoeing.

![](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Togakushi-winter-12.jpg)![Kanjiki snowshoes allow for trekking into the deeper snow in Togakushi, Nagano!](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/togakushi-kanjiki-snowshoe-3.jpg)

To make the experience truly authentic, you can use traditional Japanese snowshoes known as _kanjiki_, which have been crafted and used by locals for centuries to navigate the deep mountain drifts. One of the absolute best winter experiences in Nagano is using these snowshoes to access the famous avenue of giant cedars leading to the Okusha (Upper Shrine). Normally, this iconic path is blocked off to regular foot traffic in the winter due to the heavy snowpack, but strapping on a pair of _kanjiki_ makes it possible to safely enter the hushed, snow-covered forest for a truly magical and secluded winter experience.

You can experience kanjiki snowshoes in Togakushi as part of the tour below, paired with a soba making experience to get the best of what Togakushi has to offer!

### 5 / TOGAKUSHI NINJA MUSEUM / April to November

![](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/DSC_3441-1024x681-1.jpg)

For more than 800 years, Togakushi has had a strong association with Japan’s fabled ninjas. Established in the 12th century, the Togakure school of ninja was founded in the mountains of Togakushi which since that time was home to these most mysterious of warriors. Though practicing ninja maybe few and far between these days – believe it or not there are still some – the mountains and forests of Togakushi now play host to a ninja museum and kids village, making it a must-do activity for any aspiring ninja amongst us!

![Ninja folk museum, Togakushi](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/DSC_4575-1024x678.jpg)

Located directly across from the avenue leading to the Okusha, the [Togakure Ninpo Museum](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/?p=964) showcases the local Togakure school of ninja including exhibits of tools and weapons used. Founded by a local warrior who travelled to Iga – the traditional home of ninja – in the 12th century, Togakushi and its museum tell the story of the local school, of which, there continue to be practitioners; while the Museum of Togakushi Folklore exhibits traditional tools, clothing, furniture and other artefacts unique to the area. Visitors can try their hand at essential ninja skills such as throwing ‘shuriken’ (ninja stars) while the highlight of the museum lies in wait at the Ninja House. Rigged with secret doors, passages and traps to confuse those who enter, the aim is simple – get yourself back out of the house! The house is a true maze, equally fun for adults as it is children. The museum is open 09:00-17:00 from late-April to late-November. Admission is JPY 700.

### 13 / JOIN THE 'DONDO-YAKI' WINTER FESTIVAL / January

![Togakushi Dondo-yaki](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/c7861f33f9d953a7c324113168a9d527-2.jpg)

Every year, on the 3rd Saturday of January, the [Togakushi Dondo Yaki Festival](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/?p=1254) welcomes in the New Year. Residents of Togakushi and a relatively small crowd of visitors from elsewhere gather around a 3 metre high bonfire built out of locally-sourced green bamboo. This structure makes for quite the enchanting site when it is set alight. The ritual of burning the bamboo is said to confer good fortune on the town and all who visit it in the year ahead. After the bonfire has been lit, visitors can enjoy local delicacies such as rice cakes and 'sake 'as they watch the drum show followed by fireworks that bring this fantastic festival to a close. The festival kicks off at 7pm on the 3rd Saturday of January each year at the Togakushi Campground. As the event runs until around 10PM it's best to book a hotel in the area. Togakushi is readily accessible from Nagano Station using local bus services. Alternatively, you can use the footbridge/overpass from the second-floor of the station - accessible through the Midori shopping centre - to cross then intersection and then descend to the bus stop below.

From the Alpico bus stop, take bus numbers 70 or 71. Buses depart approximately once per hour and the journey from Nagano to the first areas of Togakushi takes approximately 50 to 60-minutes. There are several stops to choose from when you arrive including Togakushi-Hokosha (Lower Shrine), Togakushi-Chusha (Middle Shrine) and Togakushi-Okushairiguchi (Upper Shrine).  The Okushairiguchi stop is nearest to Kagami-ike (Mirror Pond) while the Chusha stop is the most convenient for those wanting to visit the Ninja Museum.

**Is it easy to get around Togakushi without a car?**

Navigating bus schedules and walking between sites can eat up your day. **Can I walk to the shrines during the winter?**

From December to March, Togakushi experiences heavy snowfall. While the lower shrines remain somewhat accessible, the famous cedar avenue leading to the _Okusha_ (Upper Shrine) is buried in deep snow and requires proper winter gear and snowshoes. For a safe, guided experience through the winter landscape, we highly recommend booking our [1-Day Togakushi Tour](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/tours), which includes transport and guided access to the snow-covered cedars.

Togakushi is famous across Japan for its soba (buckwheat noodles). The most highly-rated restaurants, such as Uzuruya, do not always take reservations and can have wait times of over an hour during peak seasons. If you want a guaranteed, immersive food experience without standing in line, our summer and autumn guided tours include a hands-on soba-making experience where you eat what you make.

**Are the ninja attractions suitable for adults?**

Yes! While the Kids' Ninja Village is primarily for younger children, the Togakure Ninpo Museum (Ninja Trick House) is highly entertaining for adults. Navigating the hidden doors and optical illusions is a genuine challenge. Our group and private tours include admission and time to explore the museum and trick house.

In the 12th century, a warrior from [Nagano](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6000.html) fled to [Iga](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4350.html) after fighting on the losing side of a war between the [Minamoto and Taira](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2132.html) clans. Iga was the traditional bedrock of the ninja, and the warrior learned his ninja skills there before returning to Nagano and starting his own ninja school.

The museum is located in the forested mountains about an hour by bus northwest of central [Nagano](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6000.html), just across the entrance to the [Upper Togakushi Shrine](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6005.html). The museum consists of multiple buildings, one of which showcases tools and weapons used by Togakure Ninja and exhibits many interesting photos of them practising techniques of warfare and infiltration.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g19/6006_02.jpg)

Gallery of photos showing Togakure ninja in action

The museum also features a **Ninja House**, a building which looks ordinary on the outside but has many secret doors, passages and contraptions on the inside. It is great fun to find the way through the excellently designed maze in the house. There is also a throwing star (shuriken) throwing range, where for a small fee visitors can try throwing shuriken at target boards.

Within the same compound stands also the **Museum of Togakushi Folklore**, which exhibits tools, clothing, receptacles and furniture used by people living in the area in the past.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g19/6006_03.jpg)

Museum of Togakushi Folklore

Express [buses](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2015.html) for tourists run every hour between Nagano Station, the Togakure Ninpo Museum and the [Togakushi shrines](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6005.html). To reach the museum, get off at the Togakushi-Okushairiguchi bus stop (戸隠奥社入口, 60 minutes, 2000 yen one way). Seat reservations should be made in advance [online](https://www.highwaybus.com/gp/inbound/inbPlanList?lineId=256) or at the Alpico Bus ticket office at Nagano Station, although it is possible to board the bus without reservation if there are vacant seats.

A separate bus operates hourly between the museum and shrines for 400 yen per ride.

## Information

The Togakushi Shrines sit in an ancient forest 40k from Hakuba. Togakushi consists of 5 Shinto Shrines connected by roads and hiking trails lined with trees all over 800 years old. It’s a stunning example of the fusion of nature and religion within Japanese culture.

```
Togakushi is only 40k from Hakuba, but it is not easily accessible by public transportation.
It is best to drive here.
```

**Ninja Museum and Ninja House**

The Togakushi area is famous for ninja and has held a ninja school from the 12th century. Today at Togakushi there is a museum where you can learn about the history of the ninja and their impact on the history of Japan.

There is also a Ninja House which at first glance looks like an ordinary home. However the Ninja House is a maze where the entrance to the next room is hidden and must be uncovered by visitors. It’s fun for adults and kids and takes about 20 minutes to complete.

**Closed from late-November to mid-April**

**Admission**: ¥650

* * *

**Kids Ninja Village**

3km from the Togakushi Forest, this Ninja Village is a small theme park perfect for kids as they can dress up as ninja and try fun ninja activities such as throwing fake throwing stars.

**Admission**: ¥500 (plus ¥300 per attraction).

* * *

**Soba**

Nagano is famous for its soba and Togakushi has a handful of restaurants serving hand-made soba and all walking distance from the Togakushi Shrines.

* * *
